lines.japanese: 「んじゃ俺、ピンフ通りのドンボルガンってとこ見てくっけど……おまえ、どうする」
lines.english: “I’m gonna go check out this Don Volgan place on Pinfu Street... What about you?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、いっしょに行ってもいいんですかー」
lines.english: “Oh—can I come with you?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、もう帰った方がいいとは思うけどさ。明日だって、朝はいつも通り早いんだろ」
lines.english: “Honestly, you should probably head home. You've still got your usual early start tomorrow, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あはー、そうですねー、家にはいられませんから」
lines.english: “Ha ha. That's true. I can't exactly stay at home.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は恥ずかしそうに、猫の後頭部へ顔を埋めた。
lines.english: Naru shyly buried her face in the back of the cat's head.

lines.japanese: ……やっぱ、まだ学校には行ってないんだな。
lines.english: ...So she still wasn't going to school.

lines.japanese: でも、それは俺みたいのがとやかく言える問題じゃない。
lines.english: But a guy like me had no business telling her what to do about that.

lines.japanese: 「おし、決めた。今日の捜索はそこ行って終わり。そこ一箇所で終わり。だからもうこの際だ、おまえも一緒に来い」
lines.english: “All right, it's settled. We check that place, and today's search is over. One last stop, that's it. So what the hell—come along.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese: 俺は命令口調で告げた。鳴は快諾し、ぴったり俺の横に並んで歩いた。
lines.english: I made it an order. Naru accepted with delight and fell into step close beside me.

lines.japanese: 信号は赤だった。夜のさなかに灯った発光ダイオードが、色彩ひとつで俺たちの前進を阻む。
lines.english: The light was red. In the dead of night, a single glowing LED barred our way with nothing but color.

lines.japanese: 「なー。おまえ、平日の昼間とかって何してんの」
lines.english: “Hey. What do you do with yourself on weekdays?”

lines.japanese: 「はー、そうですねー、５時まではたいてい区の児童館で勉強してますよー。あんまり表をぶらぶらする度胸もないですしー」
lines.english: “Let's see... Until five, I usually study at the ward children's center. I'm not really brave enough to wander around outside.”

lines.japanese: 「児童館ならいいの」
lines.english: “A children’s center is okay?”

lines.japanese: 「他の児童館は分かりませんけどー、私の通ってるところは制服のままでもお咎めないんですー。私以外にも不登校っぽいひと何人かいますしー」
lines.english: “I don't know about the others, but the one I go to doesn't mind me showing up in uniform. There are a few other kids there who look like they've stopped going to school, too.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: そういう時代なんだろうか。俺は口を閉じたまま相槌を打って、鳴からの贈り物ですこし膨らんでいるスポーツバッグを担ぎなおした。
lines.english: Maybe that's just how things are these days. I nodded without saying anything and hitched the sports bag higher on my shoulder, now bulging slightly with Naru's gifts.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ。や、べつにどーこー言うんじゃねえけどさ。ただの素朴な疑問なんだけどさ……おまえ、ずっとそうしてくつもりなの」
lines.english: “Listen. N-no, I'm not saying you gotta do this or that, okay? It's just a simple question, that's all... You planning to carry on like this forever?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、まさかー。いずれちゃんと学校行くつもりですよー」
lines.english: “Oh, no way. I’ll start going to school regularly someday.”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「まー、『いずれ』がどんどん先延ばしになっちゃってるんですけどー」
lines.english: “Though that ‘someday’ does keep getting pushed farther and farther back.”

lines.japanese: 「なんかー、もー困ったことにー、学校行こうとするとおなか痛くなったり寒気したりするんですよー、たとえ話じゃなくて本当にー」
lines.english: “The trouble is, when I try to go to school, my stomach starts hurting and I get chills. Literally—I don't mean that as a figure of speech.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、アレだろ。緊張すっと便所行きたくなるやつの深刻版みたいのだろ」
lines.english: “Oh, I know. Like a serious version of needing the bathroom when you're nervous.”

lines.japanese: 「あはー、そうかもしれないです」
lines.english: “Haha. Maybe.”

lines.japanese: 「でも最近ー、ほら私、隼人さんのおかげでなめらかに話せるようになってきたじゃないですかー」
lines.english: “But lately—well, you’ve seen how much better I’ve gotten at talking to people, thanks to you, Hayato, sir.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　そりゃべつに俺のおかげじゃねーだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? That ain't thanks to me.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、でも亜衣ちゃんと仲良くなれたのも隼人さんのおかげですしー」
lines.english: “Mmm, but it was thanks to you that I became friends with Ai, too.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それこそ俺は関係ねーだろ。おまえらが勝手に妙な意気投合しただけじゃん」
lines.english: “I had even less to do with that. You two just went and hit it off in your own weird way.”

lines.japanese: 俺がいくらそういう風に言っても、鳴は猫を抱いてくすくす笑うだけだった。
lines.english: No matter how often I told her so, Naru only hugged the cat and giggled.

lines.japanese: 俺はなんだか照れくさくて、眠そうな目をしながらほっぺの裏をつんつんした。
lines.english: I felt oddly embarrassed and pressed my tongue against the inside of my cheek, putting on a sleepy look.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーだー」
lines.english: “Oh, that’s right.”

lines.japanese: 鳴が顔を上げ、閃いたと言うにはいささか覇気のないトーンで言った。
lines.english: Naru looked up and spoke with surprisingly little energy for someone who had just had an idea.

lines.japanese: 「こんど亜衣ちゃん誘ってみようかなあ」
lines.english: “Maybe I'll invite Ai next time.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　どこに」
lines.english: “Huh? Invite her where?”

lines.japanese: 「がっこー」
lines.english: “To schooool.”

lines.japanese: 信号が青になった。進むことを許された俺たちは、前へ向かって歩きはじめた。
lines.english: The light turned green. Granted permission to proceed, we started forward.

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー、いんじゃね。つかアレ、おまえがそういうこと言うんなら、俺もやっとコレが言えるわ」
lines.english: “Yeah, sure. Why not? Hell, if you're saying stuff like that, I guess I can finally say this.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、何をですかー」
lines.english: “Say what?”

lines.japanese: 「だからアレ。がんばれ、みたいな」
lines.english: “You know. Something like... ‘You can do it.’”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ありがとうございます」
lines.english: “Yes. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、まあ、あくまでがんばれ『みたいな』だから。な。あんま無理して、学校で下痢ピーすんなよ」
lines.english: I mean, I only said something *like* ‘you can do it.’ Okay? Don't push yourself so hard you get the runs at school.

lines.japanese: 「美少女はトイレなんか行かないんです」
lines.english: “Beautiful girls don't go to the bathroom.”
“Huh?”
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: それが目に入った途端、俺と鳴はほぼ同時に口を開けていた。
lines.english: The instant we saw it, Naru and I opened our mouths almost in unison.

lines.japanese: 「背もたれ付きの……赤いチャリ……」
lines.english: “A red bike... with a backrest...”

lines.japanese: てことは──
lines.english: Which meant—

lines.japanese: 「──あれかっ！？」
lines.english: “—is that it!?”

lines.japanese: 俺は乾いた歩道を蹴った。平日の真夜中、まだ歓楽街には電飾看板がぎらぎら輝いていたけれど、ひとの数はだいぶ引けていて走りやすかった。
lines.english: I kicked off from the dry pavement. It was midnight on a weeknight, and the electric signs still blazed across the nightlife district, but the crowd had thinned enough to make running easy.

lines.japanese: 四辻の一角に立つ商業ビルの一階、スペイン料理屋を囲む植え込みの前に、その自転車は停まっていた。
lines.english: The bicycle stood before the shrubs around a Spanish restaurant on the ground floor of a commercial building at one corner of the intersection.

lines.japanese: 手の届く距離まで近付いて、俺は足を止めた。すでに店は閉まっていた。暗いガラス窓の向こうの静まりかえったフロアに、真っ赤な自転車の骨太なフレームが重なって映りこんでいた。
lines.english: I stopped within arm’s reach. The restaurant was already closed. In the dark glass, the bicycle’s sturdy red frame lay reflected over the silent dining room beyond.

lines.japanese: 俺は自転車の周囲を旋回するように移動しながら、その車体を観察した。各部位は余さずてかてかと金属の光沢を残していて、ひと目見て新品だと分かった。
lines.english: I circled the bicycle, studying it as I went. Every inch still gleamed with an unblemished metallic sheen. One look told me it was new.

lines.japanese: 遠目にはさして違和感のない普通のママチャリ風だったけれど、よくよく見ればそいつは、いささか特異な形状をしていた。背もたれ付きってこともそうだけど、それだけじゃなくて、こう──
lines.english: From a distance it passed for an ordinary city bike, but a closer look revealed a distinctly peculiar shape. There was the backrest, sure, but that wasn't all. It was more like—

lines.japanese: ──そうか、ペダルの位置が、サドルに比べて前に出すぎてるんだ。
lines.english: —right. The pedals were much too far forward relative to the saddle.

lines.japanese: ガキのころ、チャリの後ろの荷台にケツを下ろして、曲芸気分でペダルを漕いだことがあった。たぶん乗車体勢はあれに近い感じになるはず。ああ、だから背もたれが付いてるのか。
lines.english: When I was a kid, I'd sometimes plant my ass on the rear rack and pedal like I was doing a circus trick. This thing would probably put you in about the same position. Ah. So that was what the backrest was for.

lines.japanese: 「あー、私のとおんなじー」
lines.english: “Oh—it's exactly the same as mine.”

lines.japanese: 鳴が遅れてやってきた。しかしながら、口調も足取りも淡々としたものだった。俺はチャリから目を離さずに訊いた。
lines.english: Naru caught up a moment later. Her voice and footsteps, however, remained perfectly placid. Without taking my eyes off the bike, I asked,

lines.japanese: 「でも嬉しそうじゃねーな。ハズレか」
lines.english: “You don't sound too happy. Wrong one?”

lines.japanese: やつはこっくり頷いた。
lines.english: She nodded once.

lines.japanese: 「えー、型も色もまったく同じなんですけどー、私のではないですねー」
lines.english: Umm, the model and color are exactly the same, but it's not mine.

lines.japanese: 「マジで」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 屈みこんで、前輪と後輪を調べた。どちらにも錠が付いてない。高そうなチャリなのに無用心だ。
lines.english: I crouched and examined both wheels. Neither had a lock. Careless, for a bike that looked this expensive.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。でもコレ、とくに名前とか書いてないけど、おまえのと何が違うの」
lines.english: “But there's no name on it or anything. How can you tell it from yours?”

lines.japanese: 「私のこんな新品じゃないですしー、あと最初に言ったと思うんですけどー、前にこういう、カゴが付いてるんですよー」
lines.english: Mine wasn't this brand-new, and, um, I think I said at the start, mine has this kinda basket on the front.

lines.japanese: 鳴は両手を使って空に直方体を描いた。
lines.english: Naru drew a rectangular box in the air with both hands.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そういや言ってたな」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You did say that.”

lines.japanese: 俺は立ちあがってケツのほこりを払った。
lines.english: I stood up and dusted off my ass.

lines.japanese: 「でもさ。盗んだやつが、カゴはダサいから取っちゃったとか」
lines.english: But what if the thief went, ‘Baskets are lame,’ and took it off?

lines.japanese: 「えー、泣きたくなるようなこと言わないでくださいよー」
lines.english: Aww, please don't say stuff that makes me wanna cryyy.

lines.japanese: 「いや、でも、カゴぐらいで済めばまだいいじゃん。そうだよ、ちょっとおまえ、コレもっかいよく見てみろって。コレ本当におまえンじゃ──」
lines.english: “Hey, if all they took was the basket, you got off easy. Come on, take another good look. This really could be your—”

lines.japanese: ──そのとき、不意にひとの気配を感じて俺は言葉を止めた。
lines.english: —Just then, I sensed someone nearby and broke off.

lines.japanese: 殺気立った、嫌な、気配……。
lines.english: A nasty presence. Murder in the air...

lines.japanese: 体ごと振りかえった。すでに俺たちは広い半円に囲まれていた。
lines.english: I wheeled around. A broad semicircle had already formed around us.

lines.japanese: どこの陰に隠れていたのか、いずれも夜の色をした細身の野郎共が、銀色の点や線をじゃらつかせながらジワジワにじり寄ってくる。四人、五人、六人……もっとだ。
lines.english: Emerging from whatever shadows they had been hiding in, lean men dressed in the colors of night crept steadily closer, silver studs and chains jingling. Four, five, six... more.

lines.japanese: ひとりが輪のでかい重たげなチェーンを手に提げていた。口は閉じていたが、目は笑っていた。ダメージジーンズの裂け目から、傷口の下の骨を思わせる白い横糸が覗いていた。
lines.english: One of them carried a weighty chain with enormous links. His mouth was closed, but his eyes were smiling. White cross-threads showed through the rips in his distressed jeans like bone beneath a wound.

lines.japanese: なんだ、こいつら。
lines.english: What was with these guys?

lines.japanese: クソったれ。俺は鳴をさっさと終電で帰さなかったことを後悔した。
lines.english: Shit. I regretted not sending Naru home on the last train.

lines.japanese: 「え、あの……なん、なん、なんですかこれ……」
lines.english: “Um... wh-what... what is this...?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だって。心配すんなって」
lines.english: “It's okay. Don't worry.”

lines.japanese: 鳴は植え込みに阻まれるまで後ずさった。俺はスポーツバッグを足元へ落とし、やつの小さな体を隠すように両腕を広げた。
lines.english: Naru retreated until the hedge stopped her. I dropped my sports bag at my feet and spread my arms, shielding her small body behind mine.

lines.japanese: 大丈夫。このクソ共が何のつもりかは知らないけれど、そうそう乱暴な真似はできないはずだ。
lines.english: It was all right. I didn't know what these assholes were after, but they couldn't get too violent here.

lines.japanese: 多くないとは言え、まだ通りにはひとの往来がある。ソープの店先には黒服のおっさんが暇そうに立ってるし、ベンチコートをまとったカラオケ屋のあんちゃんは携帯電話と割引券を手に右往左往している。
lines.english: There were still people on the street, even if not many. A black-suited tout stood idle outside an adult bathhouse, while a karaoke hawker in a bench coat scurried to and fro, cell phone in one hand and discount coupons in the other.

lines.japanese: 俺は徐々に狭まってくる間合いを慎重に計りながら、そのパンク風に装ったガキ共を──
lines.english: I carefully watched the gap close between me and those kids dressed like punks—

lines.japanese: ──パンク風？
lines.english: —like punks?

lines.japanese: まさか、いや、ひょっとして……。
lines.english: No. It couldn’t be. Or maybe...

lines.japanese: 「うぴょーん！？　ぬゎーんだ、八木君ずゃーん！」
lines.english: “Wheee-ooop!? Whaaat, it's Yagi, darling!”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえかよ」

lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は脱力した。八つ当たりに新ピカ赤チャリを蹴倒してやりたくなったが我慢した。
lines.english: All the tension drained out of me. I wanted to kick the gleaming new red bike over out of sheer spite, but held myself back.

lines.japanese: 「なに咲夜クン、お知り合い？」
lines.english: “What's this, Sakuya? Friend of yours?”

lines.japanese: 「……って、ああ、アンタか。たしか前に、モンキの地下で会ったねェ」
lines.english: “...Oh, right. You. We met in the basement at Monki, didn't we?”

lines.japanese: いや、知らねえ。覚えてねえ。いちばん会話を交わした佐久間安男の顔さえ忘れかけてたのに、おまえみたいなキモ男ＡだかＢだかのツラなんて覚えてるわけがねえ。
lines.english: No. I didn’t know him. I didn’t remember him. I was already starting to forget the face of Yasuo Sakuma, the one I’d actually talked to most. No chance in hell I remembered the mug on some Random Creep A or B.

lines.japanese: 「ノーン、ノンノン！　みんな待て待てプリ～ズ、ジャストァたんまプリ～ン！」
lines.english: “Non, non non! Everybody wait, wait, pleeease! Just a minute, puddiiing!”

lines.japanese: 佐久間はケツをぷりぷり振りながら、両手を上げてＲなんたらの仲間たちに制止をかけた。それからウソくさい目の男とふたりして、血気に逸る仲間たちに事情を説明しているようだった。
lines.english: Waggling his ass, Sakuma raised both hands to halt his fellow R-whatevers. Then he and Shifty Eyes seemed to explain the situation to their comrades, who were spoiling for blood.

lines.japanese: 何やら「なんでだよ」「止めんなよ」「いいから殺っちゃおうよ」などという低いどよめきと、「八木君は俺のベストフレンドだプリ～ン」とかいう甲高い声とが聞こえた。
lines.english: A low murmur reached me—‘Why?’ ‘Don't stop us.’ ‘Come on, let's just kill him’—mixed with a shrill declaration that ‘Yagi is my best friend, puddiiing!’

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのーう……何が何なんです……？」
lines.english: “Um... what in the world is going on...?”

lines.japanese: 殺気ばった圧迫感が融解してゆく包囲網の内側で、いまだ事態の呑みこめない鳴が俺にしがみつきながら耳打ちした。
lines.english: Inside the ring, as its murderous pressure slowly dissolved, Naru clung to me and whispered in my ear, still unable to make head or tail of the situation.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、えーっと……だから要は、こいつらがアレ。ほら、あの掲示板の。Ｒなんたら言う」
lines.english: “Oh, uh... Basically, these are the guys. You know, from that message board. The R-whatevers.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なるほど……」
lines.english: “Oh. I see...”

lines.japanese: 語尾が下がっていく。気付かれない程度に顔を歪めていた。兄貴と同じくこの連中に良い印象を持てないのは、ひょっとして鳳家のＤＮＡと関連が……いや違うか、それが世間一般の感想か。
lines.english: Her voice sank toward the end. She was twisting her face as subtly as she could. Maybe her inability to take to these people, just like her brother’s, had something to do with Ohtori family DNA... No. That was probably society’s general opinion.

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、たしかにかなりアレな連中なんだけどダイジョブ。こっちから脅かしたりしなきゃ刺されたりしないから」
lines.english: “Yeah, they're definitely a pretty sketchy bunch, but it's okay. They're like bees: as long as we don't threaten them first, they probably won't sting us.”

lines.japanese: 鳴を安心させるために、俺はＲ－ウィング御一行をミツバチ扱いしておいた。
lines.english: To put Naru at ease, I had elected to classify the R-Wing delegation as honeybees.

lines.japanese: 「はー、そーですかー。まー、たしかにアレな方々ですけどー」
lines.english: Ohhh, I see. Well, they definitely seem like... those kinds of people.

lines.japanese: 「それに引きかえ！　ええもう先程の隼人さんはとてもすすす素敵でした。『俺がおまえを守る。この命に代えて守りぬいてみせる！』。きゃー、すてきー！　隼人すてきー！　胸が高鳴るー！」
lines.english: “By contrast! Why, Hayato, sir, you were s-s-so wonderful just now. ‘I’ll protect you. I’ll defend you with my life!’ Eee! So dreamy! Hayato, you’re so dreamy! My heart is racing!”

lines.japanese: 「すがりつくな。え、つかソレ、ちょっと脚色してね？」
lines.english: “Quit clinging to me. Wait, did you maybe embellish that a little?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、演出家の作家性により多少は台詞を──」
lines.english: “Well, the director's authorial vision called for certain liberties with the dialogue—”

lines.japanese: 「いやァ、アニキごめんごめェん！　オイラまーた同じミスしちゃったよォ、ぶひゃ！」
lines.english: “Aww, Big Bro, sorry, sorreee! I went and made the same mistake agaaain! Bwah!”
“Hmph.”

lines.japanese: ひとりずかずか近付いてきた佐久間は、俺の肩を叩きながら、鳴の視界を塞ぐような位置に立った。
lines.english: Sakuma came striding over by himself, clapped me on the shoulder, and planted himself where he blocked Naru's view of me.

lines.japanese: やつの仲間たちは状況説明を受けたらしく、みな肩透かしを食らったような表情で離れていった。またそれぞれの隠れ家に戻るのだろうか。
lines.english: His companions had apparently received the explanation. Looking thoroughly cheated of their fun, they drifted away. Maybe they were returning to their respective hiding places.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんちゃいねえホント、めんちゃい、めんちゃい！　ンだってェ？　暗くてカオよく見えなくてェ？　あとホラ隼人君もォ？　むひひ？　この前と連れてるコ違うしィ？　違うしィ？」
lines.english: “Sowwy, seriously, so sowwy, sowwy! Buuut, see? It was dark and I couldn't make out your face? And besides, Hayato, honey? Heh heh? You've got a different girl with you than last time, don't you? Don't you?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「オイオイオイ馬鹿うるせえよ、いいんだよ。余計なこと喋ってんじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, hey, you loudmouthed moron. Enough. Quit running your mouth about stuff nobody asked for.”

lines.japanese: 俺は佐久間の肩に腕をまわし、その耳元に舌打ちの連打を送りこんだ。やつはウヒヒと笑いながらバチッとウインク、片手で小指を立て、もう一方で俺の脇腹にエルボー×３を打ってきた。
lines.english: I hooked an arm around Sakuma’s shoulders and clicked my tongue loudly into his ear over and over. Cackling, he snapped me a wink, raised one pinkie, and drove his other elbow into my ribs three times.

lines.japanese: 「んイェス！　いいわァ、マジいかしてるわ八木君。んーとに男の中の男だよねェ、ぼひゃひゃ！　だってだってェ？　いッつも自分より先にオンナかばうジャン？　でしょォ、この前もそうだったでしょォ？」
lines.english: “Mm-yes! I love it, Yagi, darling. You’re seriously a man among men! Because, because—you always put yourself between the girl and danger, right? Right? You did it last time, too, didn’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「は、は？　なんと？」
lines.english: “Wh-what? What did he say?”

lines.japanese: 「だからてめえよ、あァこの糞パンク、うるせえつってんだろ。な、黙れよ。ホントまじ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ、ぶっ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “I said shut up, you piece-of-shit punk. Quiet. Seriously, I'll fucking kill you, asshole. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 俺は佐久間の脇腹にこぶしを置いてごりごりねじ回した。
lines.english: I planted a fist against Sakuma's ribs and ground it in with a slow twist.

lines.japanese: 「アーウチ、アウチ！　なァーん、なに照れてんだよ、もうこのスケコマＣ～、女たらＣ～」
lines.english: “Ow-ow, ouchie! Whaaat, why're you embarrassed, you little Casanovaaa? You lady-killerrr!”

lines.japanese: 「いいから。そういう話いいから。それより、おまえら何してんの。何なのこのチャリ」
lines.english: Enough. Enough about that. More importantly, what the hell are you guys doing? What's with this bike?

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ。餌、餌」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Bait. It’s bait.”

lines.japanese: 俺が目の前の赤いチャリンコを顎で指すと、Ｃ調パンクスはさも当然のようにへらへら笑った。
lines.english: I nodded at the red bike with my chin, and the slick punk gave me a breezy grin like the answer was obvious.

lines.japanese: 「いわゆるひとつの、イッツァおとり捜査？　ってやつゥ？　いや、ちょっと調べたらさァ、このタイプのセミリカ、地味に盗難多いとかって分かってェ」
lines.english: “It’s what you call... a classic sting operation? See, we looked into it a little, and it turns out this model of semirec gets stolen kind of a lot.”

lines.japanese: 「なにセミリカって」
lines.english: “What the hell’s a semirec?”

lines.japanese: 「セミリカンベントの略です」
lines.english: “Short for semi-recumbent.”

lines.japanese: 佐久間に訊いたら、鳴が答えた。
lines.english: I had asked Sakuma. Naru answered.

lines.japanese: 「リカンベントという、こう、仰向けで足を伸ばす感じで乗る二輪車がありまして──」
lines.english: “A recumbent is a bicycle you ride leaning back with your legs stretched out in front of you—”

lines.japanese: 「そそ、それがリカンベント。でセミリカってのは、それと普通のチャリンコの中間みたいなやつ」
lines.english: “Right, right, that’s a recumbent. And a semirec is halfway between one of those and a normal bike.”

lines.japanese: 「へ、へえー」
lines.english: “O-oh. Huh.”

lines.japanese: なんだこの空気。
lines.english: What the hell was with this tension?

lines.japanese: 「どーよ！　ねェねェ、どーよ！　アニキが探してる背もたれ付きのチャリって、コレのことでしょォ？」
lines.english: “Well? Hey, hey, what do you think? This is the bike with the backrest you're looking for, right, Big Bro?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、そうみたい──」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, seems like—”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうです」
lines.english: “Yes, it is.”

lines.japanese: 俺が訊かれたのに、鳴が答えた。
lines.english: He had asked me. Naru answered.

lines.japanese: だから、なんなんだこの空気。
lines.english: Seriously, what the hell was with this tension?

lines.japanese: いや──いや、ここは喜んでおこう。鳴も初対面の若い男相手にずいぶん突っ張れるようになったもんだ、とかって。
lines.english: No—no, I ought to be pleased. Naru had gotten much better at standing her ground with young men she’d never met. Something like that.

lines.japanese: 「ア～ニキぃ！　だからさァ、あんたが探してンのも、たぶんそういうプロのハンターに盗られたんだよ」
lines.english: “Boooss! So anyway, the one you’re looking for was probably stolen by professional hunters like that, too.”

lines.japanese: 「触んな。つーか、なにそれ。プロのハンター。はあ。なにそれ」
lines.english: “Don't touch me. And what the hell is that supposed to mean? Professional hunters? Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、調べたらさ、昔から結構いるらしンだよ。そういう屋外に置かれてる高価モンばっか狙う、せこい窃盗団みたいのって」
lines.english: Nah, we looked into it, right? Turns out there've always been these, like, cheap little theft rings that only go after expensive stuff left outside.

lines.japanese: 俺と鳴は顔を見合わせた。なるほど、と素直にこいつらの大した刑事ごっこに感心する。
lines.english: Naru and I exchanged a look. Well, hell. We were honestly impressed by their surprisingly competent detective act.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それでおとり捜査な」
lines.english: “Oh. So that's what the sting is for.”

lines.japanese: 「んイェス、イェス！　そーなの、いーでしょ、天才過ぎでしょ俺らァ！　んかか、ひとの集めた情報かっさらってくだけの、ハゲタカみてーなニワトリ共にはぜってー負けねー的スピリッツめらめら系なの俺らァ！」
lines.english: Nn-yes, yes! That's it, pretty great, right? Aren't we too damn genius?! N-kaka! We're all fired-up-spirit mode, like, no way we're losing to those vulture-ish chicken bastards who do nothing but swipe other people's intel!

lines.japanese: Ｒ－ウィング所属の小隊長殿は、腕力勝負で敗れた柳木原フレイムバーズに対し、今度は健全な対抗意識を燃やしていた。
lines.english: The R-Wing squad commander, whose troops had lost the contest of brute force to the Yanagihara Flame Birds, had found a healthier outlet for his rivalry.

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー……がんばれ」
lines.english: “Yeah, well... good luck.”

lines.japanese: どっちもがんばれ。適当にがんばれ。いい歳して番長ごっこよりは、いい歳して刑事ごっこの方がいくぶんマシだろうと思う。
lines.english: Good luck to both sides. Within reason. Grown men playing detective were marginally better than grown men playing gang boss.

lines.japanese: 「アそーそー！　そんでさァ！　こないだアニキにも、うちの隠しページ教えたッたけどさァ、うひへへへ、ゴメ～ンあそこもう捨てるわァ、つってポイッ、つって捨てちゃうわマジでェ」
lines.english: “Oh, right, right! And listen! I showed you our secret page the other day, Big Bro, but—heh heh—sorreee, we're dumping it now. Just tossing the whole thing out. For real.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、ああ、へー、そーなん」
lines.english: Uh-huh. Yeah. Wow. Is thaaat right.

lines.japanese: 俺が面倒くさげに相槌を打つと、やつはうんざりした表情で頷いた。
lines.english: I gave him a bored grunt, and he nodded wearily.

lines.japanese: 「そーりゃそーだよォ！　だってもうあそこ、グっズグズだもん！」
lines.english: “Of course! That place has gone completely to shit!”

lines.japanese: 「大司教は空気読めねーで荒し紛いンなっちゃうわ？　どこで聞きつけたんだかニワトリ連中が覗きに来やがるわ？　も、ファック！　ウザくてしょーがねンだよ死ねコラァァアあばばばばぁぁあ゛あぁあぁああ！」
lines.english: “The Archbishop can’t read a room and has practically turned into a troll! Somehow the Chicken crew found out and started peeking in! Fuck! It’s so damn annoying! Die, you bastaaards—ababababaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「うわー。うわ、うわぁー」
lines.english: “Wow. Oh. Woooow.”

lines.japanese: 唾液を滴らせて絶叫するパフォーマンスに、鳴は控えめな歓声をあげていた。さすが変なものマニア、佐久間安男という珍獣にいささかの関心を持ったようだ。
lines.english: Naru gave a restrained little cheer at the sight of him screaming with drool running down his chin. A connoisseur of strange things to the core, she seemed to have taken some interest in that rare beast, Yasuo Sakuma.

lines.japanese: 「ま、そんなワケよ。そんなワケで俺ら、あのサイトはもう捨てちゃっててェ、うん、すでにＳＮＳ中心に移行してっからァ、だからアニキも今度からはそっちに来てよ」
lines.english: Well, anyway, that's how it is. So we kinda ditched that site already, y'know, moved over mostly to social-networking sites, so you should come over there from now on too, Big Bro.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、いや、よく分かんねーけど、俺もうインターネットは卒業したから」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, well, I don't really get it, but I've graduated from the internet.”

lines.japanese: 「へ、そうなの？」
lines.english: “Huh? You did?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。まあ一時は達人だったんだけどな。でもやっぱ、アレちょー疲れるし。あとほら、目ぇ悪くすんじゃん。あのテレビ、字ぃ小さすぎじゃん」
lines.english: “Yep. I was a master for a while, but that stuff is exhausting. And it ruins your eyes, you know? The writing on that TV is way too tiny.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ああ、そう……？」
lines.english: “Oh. Uh. Right...?”

lines.japanese: 佐久間はゆるやかに首をひねった。と思ったら、すぐに首を起こした。
lines.english: Sakuma slowly cocked his head, then immediately snapped it upright again.

lines.japanese: 「あ！　じゃあ、いま言っとくけど、大司教っていやさァ」
lines.english: “Oh! Well, while I've got you here, speaking of the Archbishop—”

lines.japanese: 「俺が言うのもナンなんだけど、八木君、あんた気を付けてな？　あの馬鹿、ニワトリだけじゃなくて、あんたのこともかーなーり、恨んでるみたいだから」
lines.english: “Maybe I'm not the guy to say this, but Yagi, watch yourself, okay? That moron's got a serious grudge against you, too—not just the chickens.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺は耳を疑った。それは思ってもいない──しかし二晩続けての忠告だった。
lines.english: I could hardly believe my ears. It was the last thing I had expected—and the second warning in as many nights.

lines.japanese: 「え……だから、なんでだよ。俺、関係ねーだろ」
lines.english: “What... Why? I got nothing to do with it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は鳴に聞こえないよう、佐久間の耳を引きよせつつ声のボリュームも落とした。
lines.english: I pulled Sakuma closer by the ear and lowered my voice so Naru wouldn’t hear.

lines.japanese: 「ふざけんなよ、意味分かんねえって。あいつやったの、俺じゃなくてニワトリじゃん」
lines.english: “Don't screw with me. That makes no sense. Chicken was the one who took him down, not me.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そりゃそうだけど、でもあんとき──ほら、大司教がニワトリ撃とうとしたとき──あんた横から割って入って、ニワトリ助けちゃったじゃん」
lines.english: “Sure, that’s true. But back then—when the Archbishop tried to shoot Chicken—you jumped in from the side and saved him, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃったじゃん、って。おいおいおい。なんだよ、なんだよソレ。あんな場面に居合わせたら誰だって止めんだろフツー。なあ。そんなん逆恨みじゃねーか」
lines.english: “‘Saved him,’ you say. Come on. What the hell is that? Anybody who walked in on a scene like that would stop it. Anybody normal. He’s blaming me for his own shit.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、まったくその通りなんだけど。なんだけど、ともかくあの大司教ってのは、そういう思考回路のやつだったからさァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. You're completely right. But that's the kind of wiring the Archbishop has upstairs.”

lines.japanese: 気付けば佐久間は、例のブヒャヒャだのアバババーだのを挿まず、まるで普通の馬鹿みたいに言葉を繋げている。気味が悪い。
lines.english: At some point Sakuma had stopped peppering his speech with shrieks and cackles. He was stringing sentences together like an ordinary idiot. It was unsettling.

lines.japanese: 「なあ、ホント気ぃ付けてよ？　大司教、いま超テンパってっから。何すっか分かんねー精神状態っつーか、ぶっちゃけもう頭イカれてっから」
lines.english: “Seriously, watch yourself, okay? The Archbishop's totally freaking out right now. He's in a state where nobody knows what he'll do. Bluntly, the guy's lost his fucking mind.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、それは……知ってッけど……」
lines.english: No, I... I know...

lines.japanese: それは昨晩、俺が鳳翔に忠告したことそのままだった。
lines.english: It was the very warning I had given Kakeru Ohtori the night before.

lines.japanese: そしていま、それがそのまま返ってきた。
lines.english: And now it had come straight back to me.

lines.japanese: 俺は口をつぐんだ。かすかに胃が重かった。見えないところで自分への憎悪が育まれているという考えは面白くなかった。
lines.english: I fell silent. A faint weight settled in my stomach. There was nothing pleasant about imagining somebody’s hatred for me growing unseen.

lines.japanese: 「……なあ。あいつ、いま逃げまわってんだろ。どこにいるか、おまえら掴んでないの」
lines.english: “...Hey. He's on the run now, right? You people don't know where he is?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、掴んでねンだよ、悪りい。でも、そう遠くへは行ってねえと思うんだよ。案外いまも、すぐその辺に隠れてたりしてなァ」
lines.english: “No. Sorry, we don't. But I doubt he's gone far. Hell, he might be hiding somewhere right around here even now.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、でも、あいつ目立つから。メチャクチャその、頭といい服といいさ。だから、こっそり闇討ちとかは出来ないよね、その点は安心だ、はは」
lines.english: Yeah, but, well... the guy stands out. I mean, seriously, the hair, the clothes. So he can't exactly sneak up and jump you, right? That's one thing you can relax about. Ha.
“...You think?”

lines.japanese: いや、そんなわけはない。
lines.english: No. That wasn't true at all.

lines.japanese: 髪と服が目立つ？　だったら髪は切ればいい、服は着替えればいい。ついでにあのキモい化粧を落とせば完璧だ。
lines.english: His hair and clothes stood out? Then he could cut his hair and change his clothes. Wash off that disgusting makeup while he was at it, and the transformation would be complete.

lines.japanese: そうすれば、むしろ前の姿が強烈な印象として焼きついてる分、地味に群衆へ紛れるだけでそれ以上ない変装となるじゃないか。
lines.english: His old appearance had burned itself so vividly into people's minds that merely dressing plainly and blending into a crowd would make the perfect disguise.

lines.japanese: “案外いまも、すぐその辺に隠れてたりしてなァ”
lines.english: ‘Hell, he might be hiding somewhere right around here even now.’

lines.japanese: 佐久間の戯れ言が耳の奥にこびりついていた。
lines.english: Sakuma’s joking remark clung to the back of my mind.

lines.japanese: そうして神経質に記憶を辿っていった俺は、不意に、ヘテロのはす向かいに佇んでいたチューリップ帽の男を思いだした。表情を隠して何かを待っていた影。
lines.english: Following the thread of memory with mounting unease, I suddenly recalled the man in the tulip hat who had stood across the intersection from Hetero. A shadow with his face concealed, waiting for something.

lines.japanese: まさか……。
lines.english: It couldn't be...

lines.japanese: あの男が……？
lines.english: That man...?

lines.japanese: しかし疑ってはみても、いまの俺に確かめるすべはなかった。
lines.english: But however much I suspected him, I had no way to find out now.
